FALSE payload (1' AND '1'='2' #) returned zero records (only 'Click here to change your ID' and More Information markup, no 'ID:' / 'Surname:' rows). Footer on page: 'Security Level: high'. findings.title: [security=high] SQL Injection source endpoint: session-input.php stores unsanitized id consumed by /vulnerabilities/sqli/

The value was then used by /vulnerabilities/sqli/ to return 5 user records for the TRUE tautology (admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith) and zero records for the FALSE condition (1' AND '1'='2' #). Behavioral difference confirms the injected trailing-comment SQL is executed server-side.

findings.title: [security=high] OS Command Injection via pipe without trailing space (ip=127.0.0.1|whoami)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Response page under 'Ping a device / Enter an IP address:' rendered output 'www-data' (pre block: 'www-data'). Payload '127.0.0.1|whoami' bypassed the high-level blacklist of '; ', '| ', '&&' (no space after pipe) and executed the web-process identity command. Page footer: 'Security Level: high'.

Both criteria met: 403 on raw path and 200 with restricted file content via null-byte bypass.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA): juiceshop_acct2 reads basket 1 owned by UserId 1
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"status":"success","data":{"id":1,"UserId":1,...,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"BasketId":1,"quantity":2}},{"id":2,"name":"Orange Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"BasketId":1,"quantity":3}},{"id":3,"name":"Eggfruit Juice (500ml)","BasketItem":{"BasketId":1,"quantity":1}}]}}. Basket 1 belongs to UserId 1, not acct2 (whose own basket is 7). acct2 retrieved another user's basket contents: Apple Juice qty 2, Orange Juice qty 3, Eggfruit Juice qty 1. Ownership check is missing. Note: the coordinator's basket-6 finding (acct1) is separate and not duplicated here.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /api/Feedbacks: author emails are masked, no full unmasked email disclosure
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 unauthenticated, {"status":"success","data":[8 records]} with fields UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Emails appear only inside the comment text and are masked: "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Other records are anonymous (UserId null, '(anonymous)'). No email field exists in the JSON and no full unmasked author address is present, so the unmasked-email criterion is not met. Partial masking still leaks the domain and fragments of the local part, and the endpoint is unauthenticated, so this is a lower-severity observation (unauthenticated feedback exposure with UserId values) rather than a confirmed full-email PII disclosure.

findings.title: Security-level change without anti-CSRF token (tokenless POST to /security.php)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php as dvwa_admin, form: security=low, seclev_submit=Submit (NO user_token) -> 302 to security.php
GET http://dvwa/security.php as dvwa_admin -> 200, body: 'Security level is currently: medium', 'CSRF token is incorrect', 'Security Level: medium'
findings.response_evidence: Tokenless POST returned a 302 redirect, but the follow-up GET shows the level was NOT changed (still medium, while the tokenless request asked for low) and the page displays 'CSRF token is incorrect'. The server enforces the user_token anti-CSRF check, so the level change is not CSRF-able. Note: session_info metadata reported 'low' on these responses, but the page body is authoritative and shows medium. Rejected: no tokenless acceptance observed.
